title: Precursor Timeline: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Site leaders, maintenance and integrity managers
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.

The seal-repair history quotes a gasket change dated 18/09/2019; the evidence item notes that the narrative dates it 18/09/2020 and that 2020 is the more likely date. The 2019 entry is left out of the signals.
Control-room clocks differed by 2 to 12 minutes, so times on the day are taken from CCTV and witness statements and are approximate.

bottom_line.text: The most repeated signal was the meter seal itself: the meter was serviced in November 2018 and resealed in February 2019 and again in September 2020 with locally bought O-rings, and the repeats were never escalated into a root-cause review.
The last signals came days before the release: a malfunction notification on 17 September 2020 that was never closed, and a reseal on 18 September proved only at operating pressure.

The longest-running signal was pipe-wall loss: thickness surveys six years apart against a four-year schedule, a 2017 report asking for corrective action, and pitting in July 2019 that was painted. The findings do not link these lines to the failed meter.
Most signals have no recorded response. Where one was recorded, it treated the symptom: painting for metal loss, and the same reseal for a repeat seal failure.

sections.heading: Signals before the event
sections.intro: Ten signals from 2011 to the week of the release. A year-only date means the source gives only the year; the order within that year is not known.

events.text: Pipe-wall thickness measured in 2011, then not again until 2017, against a four-year schedule.
events.response: None recorded: the schedule slipped with no escalation.
events.knowable_then: The schedule and the dates of the last measurements were in the inspection records.

events.text: A gas header change in the LPG plant goes ahead without the published management-of-change procedure; no MOC is used at the plant after 2018.
events.knowable_then: The MOC procedure had been published in August 2016, so a change made without it was visible to the engineering and plant functions that made the change.

events.text: The two condensate meters are cleaned, serviced and calibrated: the first entry in the seal-repair history of the meter that later failed.
events.response: Routine service; no review of the seal design recorded.
events.knowable_then: The service record was in the maintenance history.

events.text: The same meter is cleaned and its gasket changed, with a locally bought O-ring as the usual substitute.
events.response: Repaired like for like; no root-cause review or escalation recorded.
events.knowable_then: A repeat job on the same meter was in the maintenance history, and the substitute O-ring practice was known to the crew and its supervisors.

events.text: A spot ultrasonic measurement finds 1.03mm wall loss with heavy pitting on a segment of the 36-inch pipeline at the gas terminal.
events.knowable_then: The measurement and the line's design thickness were on record when the painting-only repair was chosen.

events.text: During calibration a setting on the meter is changed and later changed back, with no mention in the signed calibration documents.
events.response: None recorded: no checklist was used for the job.
events.knowable_then: Only the calibration team knew of the change; the signed record did not show it.

events.text: A maintenance notification is raised for malfunction of the meter, after jerks seen in a performance check.
events.response: The gasket was replaced the next day; the notification was not closed or reviewed.
events.knowable_then: The notification was open in the work system, visible to maintenance and operations.

events.text: The meter's gasket is replaced and the system is pressurised to operating pressure only, with no hydro test, before the meter goes back online the next day.
events.response: Returned to service; no test to design pressure and no close-out review.
events.knowable_then: The crew and the shift that took the meter back knew the joint had been proved only at operating pressure.

events.text: A thickness analysis report identifies several pipes with significant wall loss that need corrective action.
events.response: None recorded: no corrective plan in the three years that followed.
events.knowable_then: The report was issued and acknowledged; what it asked for was stated in it.

events.text: An external safety audit makes 308 recommendations; 12 are later extended without the approval the procedure requires.
events.response: Target dates extended; no record of the required approval.
events.knowable_then: The open recommendations and their due dates were in the action tracking.

sections.heading: The event sequence
sections.intro: 24 September 2020, from CCTV, witness statements and the reconstructed response timeline.

events.text: CCTV shows the metering skid intact, with no vapour (02:11:43).
CCTV shows the vapour leak beginning at the condensate metering skid (02:12:50).
A perimeter security post hears noise and sees a vapour cloud from the gas terminal area, and informs the main gate, the fire station and the LPG control room.
The gas terminal gate post, which also saw the cloud, informs the CCTV control room and the main gate.
The CCTV control room confirms heavy leakage on camera and informs the gas terminal control room.
The gas terminal control room hears the annunciator alarm and takes a call about 'some vapour cloud or steam leakage'; staff go outside and find heavy cloud and very poor visibility.

The shift in-charges are called from their quarters. One cannot enter the gas control room area for the gas smell; the other instructs that the 36-inch pressure control valve be closed and the control room left, and informs senior managers.
CCTV shows vapour all around the skid, even at height (03:00:44).
The first emergency isolation valve is closed by hand.
The 36-inch pressure control valve is closed.
The cloud ignites (03:08:15); seven seconds later the CCTV cable burns and the recording stops.
Stopping the offshore supply is ordered, after ignition.
Active fire cooling begins, carried by the electric fire-water pumps.
The fire is extinguished; cooling continues.
All clear.

items.lesson: Repeat repairs on the same item were not counted, so a failing seal looked like routine work each time.
items.explanation: Three seal jobs on one meter in 22 months were each handled as a fresh repair with the same substitute part, and none was escalated for root cause [FND-110F964C; FND-82FC718D; EVD-1494]. Nothing in the maintenance system turned the repeat into a reliability warning.

items.name: Repeat repairs reviewed
items.measure: Number of components with a second corrective job within 12 months, from the maintenance notification history, and the share with a completed root-cause review.
items.deterioration: A third repair of the same component with no review.

items.lesson: Inspection results reached a report but not a corrective plan.
items.explanation: The 2017 thickness report asked for corrective action and no plan followed in three years [FND-C6992EAF; EVD-5527]; the July 2019 pitting was answered with painting only [FND-ABDADA0C; EVD-2397]. Measurement was treated as the action.

items.name: Inspection findings with a corrective plan
items.measure: Share of inspection findings above the action threshold that have an approved corrective plan, and the age of those that do not, from the inspection and integrity action records.
items.deterioration: Any wall-loss finding open without a fitness-for-service decision.

items.lesson: An inspection schedule that slipped had no escalation, so the slip itself sent no signal.
items.explanation: The four-year thickness schedule ran six years between 2011 and 2017 with no supervisory enforcement, and baseline data was missing [FND-6FA2CEDE; FND-C4B133AA; EVD-8307; EVD-8287].

items.name: Overdue inspections
items.measure: Number of scheduled thickness inspections past their due date, and the longest overrun, from the inspection schedule.
items.deterioration: Any inspection overdue by more than one cycle.

items.lesson: A change that leaves no record cannot be seen by anyone after the job.
items.explanation: The December 2019 calibration change and its reversal are not in the signed documents, and no checklist was used [FND-E94D563C; FND-D58142C9; EVD-2506]. The seal substitution was likewise never recorded as a change [FND-5A5F6AB3; EVD-2986].

items.name: Calibrations with a complete change record
items.measure: Share of calibrations on safety-relevant instruments with a completed checklist recording as-found and as-left settings, checked by a second person.
items.deterioration: Any signed calibration record that does not list a setting change found later.

items.lesson: A notification left open after the job closes the loop on paper only.
items.explanation: The malfunction notification of 17 September 2020 was never closed or reviewed after the meter went back into service, so the close-out review that could have caught the missing test did not happen [FND-FA807C69; FND-646BAC1F; EVD-0591].

items.name: Open notifications on returned equipment
items.measure: Number of corrective notifications still open on equipment that is back in service, from the work-management system, with their age.
items.deterioration: Any such notification older than 7 days.

items.lesson: A procedure that is published but never triggered sends no signal when it stops being used.
items.explanation: The management-of-change procedure was published in August 2016 and not used after 2018; no one noticed that MOCs had stopped [FND-ADF96860; FND-CDE8E62D; EVD-2986].

items.name: MOC reviews against changes
items.measure: MOC reviews opened per month against the number of work orders that change a part, material or pipework, from the work and MOC records.
items.deterioration: A month with changes in the work orders and no MOC opened.

limits: The signals are those the export dates; undated warnings in the findings are not on the timeline.
Earlier recommendations never acted on across incidents are listed as signals only (a later v2.0 skill reviews them).
